instantiated_cells.justification: The statute assigns periodic expense-statement filing to principals (not lobbyists), while lobbyists only provide information to principals for those statements, so there is no annual lobbyist-filed spending report.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; instead principals file semiannual expense statements and lobbyists merely supply information to the principal.
The statutes provided contain no requirement for any 'other' cadence of lobbyist-filed periodic spending report; reporting is via principal expense statements.
Quarterly spending reports are not required of lobbyists; the only periodic spending report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, with lobbyists supplying information.
Semiannual (Jan. 31 and July 31) expense statements are required to be filed by registered principals, not by lobbyists as separate named filers.
The provided statutes do not establish any tri-annual lobbyist-filed spending report; the reporting cadence applies to principals’ expense statements.
Itemization requirements in the periodic expense statement apply to principals’ filings, not to a separate spending report filed by lobbyists.
The periodic expense statement is filed by the principal, and lobbyists only provide supporting information to the principal, so lobbyists have no separate required spending report cadence.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is required of principals as a condition of lobbying and principal authorization, not as a separate activity report filed by lobbyists.

Compensation to lobbyists is reported within the principal’s expense statement, but the statute does not require the lobbyist to file a separate report disclosing what the lobbyist receives from clients.
The principal’s expense statement requires time records (including meeting time) but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose contacts in a separate periodic spending report.
Time spent per legislative proposal/topic is disclosed by principals in their expense statements, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Reporting of topics/legislative proposals is imposed on principals (as a condition for lobbying and authorization), not on lobbyists as separate periodic report filers.
The statute’s activity identification (legislative proposals, rules, budget subjects, topics) is a principal reporting obligation, not a lobbyist-filed periodic report.
While the principal’s expense statement covers lobbying expenditures, the law does not require lobbyists to file a separate spending report disclosing gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect (non-compensation) lobbying expenditures are reported by principals in their expense statements, not by lobbyists as separate report filers.

The statute does not require lobbyists to file itemized spending reports or disclose payments received in a lobbyist-filed periodic report; principals file the expense statements and lobbyists only submit supporting information to the principal.

Although a lobbyist license application may include the lobbyist’s primary residence address, the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report disclosing the lobbyist’s address and phone number.

The law requires principals (not lobbyists) to report legislative proposals, rules, budget subjects, or topics connected to lobbying communications, so lobbyists are not required to file an activity report.
Disclosure requirements in the periodic expense statement are imposed on principals, and there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requiring disclosure of the principal’s business nature.

Principal identity and address are disclosed through principal registration and authorizations, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate periodic spending report disclosing principals’ address/phone.
Authorizations to represent a principal are filed with the commission, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report listing all principals represented.
Identification of legislative proposals and proposed administrative rule numbers is reported by principals, not by lobbyists in a separate periodic spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are required components of the principal’s expense statement, but lobbyists are not required to file a separate disclosure report.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by principals in the principal’s expense statement, not by lobbyists in a separate periodic spending report.

Because the statute assigns periodic spending disclosure to principals and requires lobbyists only to provide supporting information, there is no requirement for lobbyists to file itemized spending reports and/or compensation disclosures as separate filers.
The periodic filing obligation applies to principals’ expense statements, and the statute does not impose on lobbyists any separate 'no activity' spending report requirement.

The principal’s expense statement does not require lobbyists to file any separate report and does not specify reporting of lobbyist spending on household members of public officials as a lobbyist-filed disclosure item.
Any itemization requirements in the periodic expense statement apply to principals’ filings, and there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report that would be itemized.
